news.title: Viem vs. Ethers.js: A Detailed Comparison for Web3 Developers
news.subtitle: This blog explores the differences, benefits, and trade-offs between Ethers.js and Viem for building dapps on Ethereum

childMarkdownRemark.html:
When building dapps on Ethereum, choosing the right library can significantly impact your development process and project success. Two prominent libraries in this space are Ethers.js and Viem. Both offer a powerful set of tools for connecting to smart contracts, sending transactions, and querying blockchain data with official support for TypeScript. Both libraries also adopt a modular design, allowing for the selective inclusion of library parts to optimize bundle size and application performance.

In this blog post, we'll explore these libraries in detail, highlighting their key differences, benefits, and trade-offs, as well as when to use one over the other. In the end, you should have all the information you need to decide when starting your next project.

The key difference between Ethers.js and Viem


While they share a common goal, Ethers.js and Viem differ significantly in their approach and features, catering to varied developer preferences and project requirements.

Ethers.js


  • Providers in Ethers.js: Ethers.js uses providers as a bridge to the Ethereum network. These providers are versatile objects through which developers can read blockchain data or send transactions. Ethers.js simplifies the connection process to various Ethereum nodes via multiple provider types, including default, JSON-RPC, and Infura providers. This abstraction allows developers to concentrate more on their dapp's functionality rather than on the complexities of network connection.
  • Maturity and Stability: Ethers.js offers a long history and a robust support community, making it a reliable choice for complex projects. With a comprehensive feature set, it provides a wide range of functionalities, ideal for developers seeking a one-stop solution for Ethereum interaction. Despite its comprehensive nature, Ethers.js maintains a modular design, allowing developers to pick and choose specific functionalities.

Viem


  • Actions with Viem: Viem introduces the concept of actions — functions dedicated to executing specific tasks on the Ethereum network. These can be categorized into public actions (like retrieving a transaction) and wallet actions (such as sending a transaction). Designed for composability and modularity, Viem's actions enable developers to craft Ethereum applications with greater clarity and efficiency.
  • Efficiency and Minimalism: Viem focuses on a minimalist design, optimizing for efficiency with a smaller bundle size and selective execution of tasks. It emphasizes modularity and composability through its APIs, enabling a leaner, more efficient development process. With an innovative approach, Viem aims for a straightforward API design, prioritizing clarity and ease of use to enhance the developer experience.

Choosing between Ethers.js and Viem


Choosing between Ethers.js and Viem depends on the specific needs of your project and your preferences as a developer.

  • Ethers.js is best suited for projects that demand a comprehensive set of features and prioritize maturity and community support. It's ideal for complex dapps requiring extensive interaction with the Ethereum network.
  • Viem is the go-to choice for projects where efficiency, a lightweight bundle, and a minimalist design are key considerations. It shines in web applications focused on speed and performance, as well as for developers who prefer a modular and innovative approach to Ethereum interaction.

Benefits and Tradeoffs of Ethers.js and Viem


Ethers.js


Benefits:

  • Broad range of features and strong community support.
  • High stability and reliability derived from its maturity.

Tradeoffs:

  • Potentially overwhelming for projects that do not require its extensive feature set.
  • Managing dependencies and external providers can add complexity.

Viem


Benefits:

  • Efficient and lightweight, perfect for performance-sensitive applications.
  • Simplifies the development process with its modular design and clear documentation.

Tradeoffs:

  • Less mature than Ethers.js, with a smaller community and fewer resources.
  • May require more effort to manage due to its unopinionated, modular nature.

Technical differences between Ethers.js and Viem


Below is an enhanced comparison table between Ethers.js and Viem, featuring code examples and brief explanations for various functionalities. This comparison highlights the structural and conceptual differences in how each library approaches interactions with the Ethereum blockchain.

Other things to keep in mind


Terminology and Conceptual Clarity: The term "provider" is widely used in web3 development but can often lead to confusion due to its overloaded meaning. Viem addresses this by employing the term "Client," categorizing them into Public Client (for blockchain information access), Wallet Client (for transaction signing), and Test Client (for local node testing). This distinction helps developers better navigate the Ethereum interaction landscape.

Bundle Size and Efficiency: Viem is designed with a minimalist modular architecture, boasting a bundle size of only 35kB. This contrasts sharply with Ethers.js, which, due to its broader range of built-in functionalities, results in a larger bundle size and potentially impacts web application performance more significantly.

API Design and Development Experience: Viem opts for verbose APIs, prioritizing flexibility and ease of change. This approach stands in contrast to Ethers.js, which may employ more abstracted APIs for some functionalities, potentially making it harder to modify or extend the codebase. Additionally, leveraging TypeScript, Viem provides strongly typed APIs, enhancing the development experience through features like autocomplete, type inference, and static validation. This reduces the chance of runtime errors and makes the API more intuitive.

Conclusion


Each library offers a distinct approach to interacting with the Ethereum blockchain. Ethers.js tends to abstract complexities through predefined classes and methods, aiming for an object-oriented experience. In contrast, Viem opts for a more function-driven interface, emphasizing explicitness and perhaps offering a slightly steeper learning curve but greater flexibility in certain contexts.

Ethers.js is geared towards developers seeking a comprehensive toolkit for complex dApps, offering a rich set of abstractions and functionalities. On the other hand, Viem caters to those who value efficiency, modularity, and a minimalist design, providing a streamlined and innovative approach to Ethereum development. The choice between the two ultimately rests on the developer's or project's specific requirements and preferences.

childMarkdownRemark.html:

🦊 What we’ve been up to 🦊

A phish on a fork, no chips

Highlighting the first release of @lavamoat/node, Naugtur explores a sneaky security risk in GitHub development. Attackers are creating malicious forks of popular repositories and slipping in harmful code. Even if you've been following the development of LavaMoat you probably did not see @lavamoat/node coming. However, it's a major rewrite that was necessary to bring in enterprise service management (ESM) support.

AnChain.AI x MetaMask Snaps: protect your transactions

In this X Space, AnChain.AI discusses its MetaMask Snap that allows more people to benefit from easier access to the data they aggregate on bad actors. The algorithm they built assesses the risk to transactions, wallets, and smart contracts.

Christian Montoya said about Snaps more broadly: "Through the Snaps platform, we're able to connect with a lot of different teams that are working in the security space. Because they can launch their own Snaps, they can demonstrate their capabilities to protect against malicious activity, to help decode transactions, and to do better simulations."

Christian also teased that MetaMask is exploring ways to leverage AI to make users more secure.

Improvements to signature request readability

This month, we launched new, consistent, and more readable transactions and signatures on MetaMask Extension. The improvements will be coming to MetaMask App on mobile very soon.

🎙️ MetaMask in the security ecosystem 🔎

Using LavaMoat to block malicious postinstalls

It's Naugtur again, and this time he raised the alarm for Rspack users — a Rust-based JavaScript bundler — who may have unknowingly installed a malicious release. Fortunately, the issue was swiftly addressed, but tools like LavaMoat can help developers stay protected from similar supply chain attacks in the future.

North Korea hack group may be behind $70 Million Phemex exploit, experts say...

And one of these experts is MetaMask's Taylor Monahan. Over $70M in crypto was stolen from Singapore-based exchange Phemex. According to Taylor, the attack's complexity indicates involvement by a seasoned group, possibly linked to North Korea. The attackers swiftly drained a wide array of assets across multiple blockchains, converting them into native tokens like ETH and BTC. She noted that the manual execution of numerous transactions across various chains suggests the work of experienced threat actors. This method mirrors tactics previously associated with North Korean hacking groups, such as the Lazarus Group.

Meanwhile...

Chainalysis releases Crypto Crime Report for 2025

Chainalysis's annual Crypto Crime Report has landed. While you wait for your copy to arrive, get a sneak peek by reading an excerpt – Illicit Volumes Portend Record Year as On-Chain Crime Becomes Increasingly Diverse and Professionalized, here.

⚠️ Tales of Caution⚠️

Fake homebrew Google Ads target Mac users with malware

Summary

Hackers have launched a malware campaign via Google Ads, targeting users of the Homebrew package manager for macOS and Linux with a counterfeit website. The campaign distributes AmosStealer, a malware designed to steal credentials, browser data, and cryptocurrency data by masquerading as a legitimate Homebrew site. Security experts have highlighted the campaign's sophistication and potential to harm unsuspecting users significantly.

How Users Can Protect Themselves

Always verify the authenticity of websites before downloading any software or entering personal information. Be cautious of Google ads that lead to external sites, especially those that look similar to legitimate services like Homebrew. Consider bookmarking official websites you frequently visit to avoid falling for fake ads. Additionally, follow reputable cybersecurity experts and updates to stay informed about the latest threats.

Navigating the Contagious Interview malware campaign

Summary

Contagious Interview, a DPRK-affiliated cyber threat group active since December 2022, has been exploiting the cryptocurrency industry through sophisticated social engineering attacks. They lure victims with fake job offers or freelance development work, only to infect their devices with BeaverTail infostealer malware via malicious code distributed through platforms like GitHub and Bitbucket. This malware targets crypto assets, draining browsers and desktop wallets soon after installation. The group employs a second payload, InvisibleFerret, to further compromise devices for ongoing exploitation.

How Users Can Protect Themselves

Individuals should exercise caution when approached with job offers on social media, verifying the authenticity of recruiter profiles and avoiding suspicious links or scripts. They should also use antivirus software and keep personal and work activities separate, possibly on different machines or virtual environments. Organizations can protect themselves by educating employees on phishing tactics, enforcing strict device policies, and using secure channels for recruitment processes.

AdsPower supplychain attack leads to $3M stolen in ETH

Summary

ADSPower, an anti-detect browser, fell victim to a hacking incident that resulted in the theft of over $3M in crypto assets from over 34,000 wallets. The breach was first hinted at on January 23, with users reporting issues with MetaMask within ADSPower on various Telegram crypto chats. By January 25, a significant withdrawal of funds from users' wallets was observed, and the ADSPower team acknowledged the breach. The attack was executed by replacing legitimate wallet extensions with fraudulent ones, deceiving users into submitting their seed phrases and passwords.

How users can protect themselves

If you're an ADSPower user, and installed or updated the MetaMask extension between January 21 and January 24, take immediate action to secure your assets and account: delete the current MetaMask Extension, and any other wallet extensions you suspect might be compromised. Reinstall them directly from the Chrome Web Store to ensure that you're using the authentic versions.

Move your crypto-assets to a new wallet. When setting up the new wallet, import your seed phrases or private keys directly, and avoid using ADSPower during this process to prevent potential exposure to malicious software. Contact ADSPower's support team at support@adspower.com. Provide them with details and any proof of compromise to get assistance and potentially help prevent further breaches.

Looking for more? Head here to peruse previous editions of Luker's MetaMask Security Reports.

nodes.title: How to bridge crypto
nodes.subtitle: Easily move your tokens across chains.

image.title: How to bridge crypto with MetaMask
image.description: How to bridge crypto with MetaMask wallet

childMarkdownRemark.html:
You know the drill. You’ve got 200 in ETH on Ethereum, and you want to bridge it to USDC on Linea. In lesser hands, this process could be clunky and time consuming. With MetaMask wallet, bridging crypto is as easy as can be.

Our aggregator finds you fast, cost-effective routes to move your tokens from one chain to another. And with cross-chain swapping, bridging and swapping can take place at the same time in a single transaction. Meaning: you can swap a token from one chain to a different token on another chain all in one move. Bada-bing, bada-boom.

Below, you’ll find step-by-step guides showing you how to bridge crypto with MetaMask on desktop and mobile.

Let’s get into it! 🦊

How to bridge crypto with MetaMask Extension

  1. Click Bridge to get started.
  2. Select the network and token you want to bridge from. Example: ETH on Ethereum.
  3. Select the network and token you want to bridge to. Example: USDC on Linea.
  4. Enter the amount you want to send to load quotes. Example: 0.1 ETH.
  5. Select the recommended route presented to you, or select another option by clicking on More Quotes.
  6. Click Submit to confirm your bridge transaction in your MetaMask wallet.
  7. Your transaction will be submitted and confirmed shortly after. You’ll be able to view your assets on the new chain.

Success! 🦊

How to bridge crypto with MetaMask App

  1. Sign-in to MetaMask App.
  2. Tap the menu button, which has two arrows in opposite directions and is located on the bottom of your homepage screen.
  3. Tap Bridge. Note: You will be taken to the Bridge feature on MetaMask Portfolio.
  4. Select the network you want to bridge from. Example: Ethereum.
  5. Select the token you want to bridge and enter the amount you want to send. Example: 0.1 ETH.
  6. Select the network you want to bridge your tokens to. Example: Linea.
  7. Select the token you want to receive on your destination network. Example: USDC.
  8. Select the recommended route presented to you, or select another option by clicking on Choose a different quote.
  9. Click Confirm to confirm your bridge transaction in your MetaMask wallet.
  10. You’ll be able to keep track of your transfer with the Bridging in progress bar — and view your assets on the new chain.

Success! 🦊

Ready to get started? If you’re on desktop, download MetaMask Extension. If you’re on mobile, download MetaMask App for iOS or Android.

Need more help? We got you. Check out our MetaMask Support guide for detailed info about bridging crypto.

childMarkdownRemark.html:
Swapping crypto is fast, easy, and secure with MetaMask. You can choose from thousands of your favorite tokens across nine networks including Ethereum, Linea, Base, and Arbitrum. MetaMask Swaps also include gas fees right in your quotes, making swapping crypto as smooth as can be.

We've simplified cross-chain swapping too. Send&Swap lets you choose the token you want to spend and the token you want the other person to receive — all in one move. As ever, safety is essential when it comes to your digital assets. So rest easy. MetaMask Swaps are powered by our razor-tight, industry-leading security.

Below, you'll find step-by-step guides showing you how to swap crypto with MetaMask.

Let’s get into it! 🦊

How to swap crypto with MetaMask Extension

  1. Open the MetaMask browser extension.
  2. Select the network you want to swap on, and click the Swap button.
  3. Select the token you want to swap from. Example: ETH.
  4. Enter the amount that you want to swap.
  5. Select the token you want to swap to. Example: DAI.
  6. A preferred quote will be loaded automatically. To select a different quote, click View all quotes.
  7. Click Swap to confirm.

Success! 🦊

How to swap crypto with MetaMask App

  1. Sign-in to your MetaMask mobile app.
  2. Select the network you want to swap on, located at the top of your screen. Example: Ethereum Mainnet.
  3. Tap the menu button, which has two arrows in opposite directions and is located on the bottom of your homepage screen.
  4. Tap Swap.
  5. Select the token you want to swap from by tapping the token name that appears under your wallet address. Example: ETH.
  6. Enter the amount that you want to swap.
  7. Select the token you want to swap to. Example: DAI.
  8. Tap Get quotes to proceed. Note: you can manually select a different quote from our range of industry-leading providers.
  9. Tap Swap to confirm.

Success! 🦊

How to swap crypto with MetaMask Portfolio

  1. Connect your MetaMask wallet to portfolio.metamask.io
  2. Click Move crypto.
  3. Click Swap.
  4. Select the network you want to swap from in the dropdown menu. Example: Ethereum.
  5. Select the token you want to swap from. Example: ETH.
  6. Enter the amount that you want to swap.
  7. Select the token you want to swap to. Example: DAI.
  8. Click Get Quotes to proceed. Note: you can manually select a different quote from our range of industry-leading providers.
  9. Click Swap to confirm.

Success! 🦊

Ready to start swapping crypto? If you’re on desktop, download MetaMask Extension. If you’re on mobile, download MetaMask app for iOS or Android.

Need more help? We got you. Check out our MetaMask Support guide about swapping crypto.
